chunks: Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Baghdadi narrated that he heard Abu Umar, the companion of Abu al-Abbas Tha'lab, was asked about the meaning of his (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'I am leaving among you the Two Heavy Things.' He was asked: 'Why are they called the Two Heavy Things?'
He replied: 'Because adhering to them is heavy/difficult.'

key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْنِ: The Two Heavy Things (referring to the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Why are the Quran and Ahl al-Bayt referred to as the 'Two Heavy Things' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the linguistic nuance that the 'heaviness' of the Two Entities refers to the rigorous effort and steadfastness required to adhere to their guidance, rather than physical weight. In Shia scholarship, this interpretation underscores the profound responsibility placed upon the community to maintain fidelity to the Prophet and his progeny, framing their leadership as a demanding yet essential spiritual anchor.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-26 Ali ibn Al-Fadhl al-Baghdadi narrated that he had heard that Abu Umar - the friend of Abil Abbas Tha’lab was asked the following question regarding the meaning ‘I will leave two heavy things with you’ that the Prophet (s) said. He was asked, ‘Why are these two things called heavy things?’
He replied, ‘Since they are very hard to adhere to.’
